title: Genesis 25: Two Nations in the Womb
body:
Read the chapter → [Genesis 25](/bible/genesis/25)

**[Genesis 25:1-6](/bible/genesis/25#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/genesis/25#v1)</sup> Then again Abraham took a wife, and her name was Keturah.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/genesis/25#v2)</sup> And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/genesis/25#v3)</sup> And Jokshan begat Sheba, and Dedan. And the sons of Dedan were Asshurim, and Letushim, and Leummim.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/genesis/25#v4)</sup> And the sons of Midian; Ephah, and Epher, and Hanoch, and Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the children of Keturah.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/genesis/25#v5)</sup> And Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/genesis/25#v6)</sup> But unto the sons of the concubines, which Abraham had, Abraham gave gifts, and sent them away from Isaac his son, while he yet lived, eastward, unto the east country.

- Abraham took Keturah and had more sons, but Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac; to the sons of the concubines he gave gifts and sent them away eastward from Isaac. The inheritance followed the child of the promise.

**[Genesis 25:7-10](/bible/genesis/25#v7)**

> <sup>[7](/bible/genesis/25#v7)</sup> And these are the days of the years of Abraham’s life which he lived, an hundred threescore and fifteen years.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/genesis/25#v8)</sup> Then Abraham gave up the ghost, and died in a good old age, an old man, and full of years; and was gathered to his people.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/genesis/25#v9)</sup> And his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, which is before Mamre;
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/genesis/25#v10)</sup> The field which Abraham purchased of the sons of Heth: there was Abraham buried, and Sarah his wife.

- Abraham lived an hundred threescore and fifteen years and died in a good old age, as it was prophesied to him; his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah with Sarah.

**[Genesis 25:12-18](/bible/genesis/25#v12)**

> <sup>[12](/bible/genesis/25#v12)</sup> Now these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s handmaid, bare unto Abraham:
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/genesis/25#v13)</sup> And these are the names of the sons of Ishmael, by their names, according to their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebajoth; and Kedar, and Adbeel, and Mibsam,
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/genesis/25#v14)</sup> And Mishma, and Dumah, and Massa,
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/genesis/25#v15)</sup> Hadar, and Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah:
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/genesis/25#v16)</sup> These are the sons of Ishmael, and these are their names, by their towns, and by their castles; twelve princes according to their nations.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/genesis/25#v17)</sup> And these are the years of the life of Ishmael, an hundred and thirty and seven years: and he gave up the ghost and died; and was gathered unto his people.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/genesis/25#v18)</sup> And they dwelt from Havilah unto Shur, that is before Egypt, as thou goest toward Assyria: and he died in the presence of all his brethren.

- The generations of Ishmael list twelve princes according to their nations, exactly as the Most High promised in [Genesis 17:20](/bible/genesis/17#v20). Ishmael lived an hundred and thirty and seven years and died in the presence of all his brethren.

**[Genesis 25:20-21](/bible/genesis/25#v20)**

> <sup>[20](/bible/genesis/25#v20)</sup> And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Syrian of Padan–aram, the sister to Laban the Syrian.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/genesis/25#v21)</sup> And Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren: and the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah his wife conceived.

- Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife. Brothers waiting on a wife, be patient and stay virtuous; Isaac waited forty years, and the Most High had the right sister appointed.
- Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife because she was barren, and the Lord was intreated of him; Rebekah conceived.

**[Genesis 25:22-23](/bible/genesis/25#v22)**

> <sup>[22](/bible/genesis/25#v22)</sup> And the children struggled together within her; and she said, If it be so, why am I thus? And she went to enquire of the Lord.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/genesis/25#v23)</sup> And the Lord said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.

- The children struggled together within her, and the Lord gave Rebekah the prophecy: two nations are in thy womb, one people stronger than the other, and the elder shall serve the younger.
- The whole scripture is good set against evil: the godly against the sinner, Jacob against Esau, righteousness against sin. Two powerful forces were being born into the earth, and the struggle began in the womb.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ecclesiasticus 33:14-15](/bible/sirach/33#v14)**
    > <sup>[14](/bible/sirach/33#v14)</sup> Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.
    >
    > <sup>[15](/bible/sirach/33#v15)</sup> So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.

    Good is set against evil and the godly against the sinner; all the works of the Most High are two and two, one against another.

**[Genesis 25:24-26](/bible/genesis/25#v24)**

> <sup>[24](/bible/genesis/25#v24)</sup> And when her days to be delivered were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/genesis/25#v25)</sup> And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/genesis/25#v26)</sup> And after that came his brother out, and his hand took hold on Esau’s heel; and his name was called Jacob: and Isaac was threescore years old when she bare them.

- The first came out red, all over like an hairy garment, and they called his name Esau. The scriptures describe the man because a nation comes from him; this teaching identifies Esau's seed with the red, hairy, melanin-lacking people of the world today.
- Jacob's hand took hold on Esau's heel, and that is prophecy: Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth. When Esau's rulership is done, Jacob comes into power; that is how we know the times.

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Esdras 6:7-9](/bible/2-esdras/6#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/2-esdras/6#v7)</sup> Then answered I and said, What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/2-esdras/6#v8)</sup> And he said unto me, From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/2-esdras/6#v9)</sup> For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.

    Jacob's hand held first the heel of Esau; Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of it that followeth.

**[Genesis 25:27-28](/bible/genesis/25#v27)**

> <sup>[27](/bible/genesis/25#v27)</sup> And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/genesis/25#v28)</sup> And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.

- Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents. The Most High gives you the characteristics of the man so the nation can be known.
- Isaac loved Esau because he did eat of his venison, but Rebekah loved Jacob, because the Lord had told her the prophecy that the younger was the chosen.

**[Genesis 25:29-34](/bible/genesis/25#v29)**

> <sup>[29](/bible/genesis/25#v29)</sup> And Jacob sod pottage: and Esau came from the field, and he was faint:
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/genesis/25#v30)</sup> And Esau said to Jacob, Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint: therefore was his name called Edom.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/genesis/25#v31)</sup> And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/genesis/25#v32)</sup> And Esau said, Behold, I am at the point to die: and what profit shall this birthright do to me?
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/genesis/25#v33)</sup> And Jacob said, Swear to me this day; and he sware unto him: and he sold his birthright unto Jacob.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/genesis/25#v34)</sup> Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.

- Esau sold his birthright for red pottage; therefore was his name called Edom, red. He said, What profit shall this birthright do to me, and sware it away for a meal.
- Thus Esau despised his birthright. Jacob is called a supplanter, but the supplanting was of the Holy Ghost; Esau gave the birthright away himself.
